semantics.clock: All t values are seconds since observer install; original session.started_at is on the same monotonic clock.
semantics.chat: _chat_completion entry to original return/exception: includes payload build, retries, stream consumption and parsing. Includes summary calls; tools_present only labels whether a tools argument is supplied, not the call's purpose.
semantics.http: Entry to existing requests.post, then original return/exception. A streamed return may contain only headers; this does not measure server decode or full generation latency. No body/headers/payload is inspected.
semantics.gate_wait: Original _enqueue_and_wait entry to normal return, under the existing Condition: includes enqueue/pump/wait/wakeup, not just Condition.wait sleep. Admission is caller-observed ownership, not the earlier pump selection instant.
semantics.release: handover: enqueue entry immediately after original _free increment; final release: pump entry immediately after original _free increment. Neither hook performs release itself.
semantics.slot_held: Sum of admitted-return to release-credit intervals; includes model calls, Python work and idle time while the game owns a slot. Open intervals are reported separately.
semantics.tokens: Usage on successful original _chat_completion result only; null when absent. Partial/failed generation is unknown, not zero. No counters in the solver are changed.
semantics.boundedness: At most max_sessions ledgers; newest max_events_per_session events each. First timestamps and all-event aggregate counters survive event eviction.
semantics.threading: No added locks. Session ledgers have one play-thread writer; snapshot after drain for final consistency. Calls outside an observed play/chat scope pass through.

microbenchmark.boundary: Synthetic CPU request construction + fake response; observer spy adds a list append. Not GPU/model/server/real network latency.

boundaries: Actual tool_agent._chat_completion and actual _PriorityGate, custom Session wrapper scope.
All transport replaced by controlled fake responses; real Session.request raises.
JSON and SSE reads belong to the original method, verified once; no model/GPU used.
Priority ordering was controlled with two threads and one slot, not a full scheduler benchmark.
No engine implementation read and no solver/source runtime file changed.
